title: A Tajik Bank Shuts Side Door for Russian Cardholders
gist: Tajikistan's Humo Bank told Russian clients their cards would be blocked on October 1 unless they completed in-person biometric identification in Tajikistan by September 30, effectively closing a remotely opened card channel used by non-residents. The bank cites fraud protection, but a client reports it is restricting 'certain categories of non-resident individuals' with online-opened cards.

themes.theme: Humo Bank card cutoff for Russians

insights.claim: Tajikistan's Humo Bank warned Russian clients their cards would be blocked on October 1 unless they visited a Humo office in Tajikistan by September 30 for biometric identification, advising them to move balances to ruble cards.
insights.so_what: Closure of Central Asian card 'side doors' narrows Russians' options for foreign-currency payments abroad under sanctions, a sign of tightening compliance in the region.
insights.quote: If you can’t come to Tajikistan in person and complete the identification, unfortunately, your card will be closed
insights.speaker: Kulobiddin Norov

insights.claim: Humo Bank offered affected Russians a replacement card only if they travel to Tajikistan, valid only for the duration of their legal stay and no longer than a year.
insights.so_what: The new terms effectively end remote card ownership by non-residents, eliminating the bank's use as an offshore payment channel for Russians.
insights.quote: valid only for the duration of her legal stay and for no longer than a year
insights.speaker: Kulobiddin Norov

insights.claim: Humo Bank officially cited fraud protection, but its support staff told a Russian client it was restricting services for 'certain categories of non-resident individuals' whose cards were opened online.
insights.so_what: The targeting of online-opened non-resident cards suggests de-risking pressure, possibly sanctions-related, rather than generic fraud control.
insights.speaker: Kulobiddin Norov

insights.claim: A Russian Humo Bank client said a transfer of about 300 euros had been stuck for a week and the bank stopped responding to her complaints.
insights.so_what: Frozen transfers illustrate counterparty and access risk for Russians relying on third-country banks for euro payments.
insights.speaker: Kulobiddin Norov
